commands.review_summary:
The PR replaces raw description slicing in `buildWorkspaceSkillCommandSpecs` with `truncateUtf16Safe` for workspace skill and Claude bundle command descriptions, plus focused regression tests.

PR surface: Source +1, Tests +59. Total +60 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. from source inspection: current `main` cuts descriptions with raw `slice(0, 99)`, so a description with 98 ASCII code units followed by an emoji leaves a dangling high surrogate. I did not execute a repro because this review was constrained to read-only inspection.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A repair worker can make the bundle regression test exercise the actual bundle-command branch without changing product behavior or needing maintainer product judgment.

target.title: fix(skills): keep command spec descriptions UTF-16 safe at the truncation cut
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where skill command descriptions in `/help` and tool inventory could render a broken character when a description containing an emoji or other astral-plane Unicode character was truncated at the exact surrogate-pair boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two description truncation sites in `buildWorkspaceSkillCommandSpecs` (workspace skills line 135 and bundle commands line 206) now use the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper instead of raw `String.prototype.slice`. The helper adjusts the cut point when it would split a UTF-16 surrogate pair, keeping the same character-count budget while avoiding dangling surrogate halves in user-visible command text. No new abstraction — `truncateUtf16Safe` already exists in `src/shared/utf16-slice.ts` and is used by sibling callers (`src/agents/tool-description-summary.ts`, `src/auto-reply/chunk.ts`).

## User Impact

Skill command descriptions containing emoji or astral Unicode now truncate cleanly without dangling surrogates. The fix covers both workspace skills and bundled Claude commands.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** UTF-16-safe truncation of skill command descriptions at the 99-character boundary when an emoji straddles the cut point.

**Real environment tested:** Node.js v22.22.0, actual `buildWorkspaceSkillCommandSpecs` exported function with real `SkillEntry` objects. No vitest mock of the function under test — the proof imports and calls the production export directly.

**Evidence after fix (9 passed, 0 failed):**

```
[case 1] workspace skill: emoji at surrogate-pair boundary (prefix=98)
  description length: 99 chars
  ends with ellipsis: true
  has replacement char: false
  has dangling surrogate: false
  ok: no replacement char
  ok: no dangling surrogate
  ok: truncation marker present
  ok: emoji excluded cleanly (starts with 98 a)

[case 2] bundle command: emoji at surrogate-pair boundary (prefix=98)
  ok: no dangling surrogate
  ok: starts with expected prefix
  description length: 99 chars

[case 3] short description: no truncation (regression guard)
  description: "short 😀 desc"
  ok: short description unchanged

[case 4] workspace+emoji within limit (prefix=97, emoji fits)
  description length: 100 chars
  has emoji: true
  ok: emoji preserved intact
  ok: no dangling surrogate

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

**Negative control (pre-fix main code, same script, same environment):**

```
[case 1] workspace skill: emoji at surrogate-pair boundary (prefix=98)
  FAIL: no dangling surrogate
  has dangling surrogate: true
  description length: 100 chars  (vs 99 after fix — includes orphan surrogate)

[case 2] bundle command: emoji at surrogate-pair boundary (prefix=98)
  FAIL: no dangling surrogate
  description length: 100 chars

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 7 passed, 2 failed
exit=1
```

**Quantified impact:** With prefix=98 ASCII chars + `😀` (2 UTF-16 code units starting at positions 98–99), the old `slice(0, 99)` produces a 100-char string whose last visible codepoint is the orphan high surrogate `\uD83D`; downstream systems render it as `�`. The fix produces a 99-char string that cleanly excludes the entire surrogate pair. When the emoji fits within the limit (prefix=97, total 99 UTF-16 code units ≤ 99), the fix preserves the emoji intact.

## Evidence

**Focused tests:**

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/discovery/command-specs.test.ts
Tests  3 passed (3)
```

**Lint:** `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` clean on both changed files.

**Typecheck:** `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json` clean.

**Format:** `oxfmt --check` clean on both changed files.
